evidence.note: Repeated whole-workspace `cargo test --workspace --tests --no-run` milestone checks (255,267,275,295,300,375) plus `--no-fail-fast` (381,507) — deliberate horizon checks that surface full pass/fail across all binaries rather than first-failure, indicating tracking of how much of the suite is green.

Repeated per-crate `--no-fail-fast` runs on controller-manager (413,428,430,486,504) show it recognized that crate as the largest remaining gap and kept returning to it — noticing a stuck/dominant crate rather than losing the plot.
After editing the leaf `common` crate it re-runs `cargo test --workspace --tests --no-run`, checking that downstream/earlier crates still build — regression-awareness on previously-green work.

Late-game targeted single-binary runs (`--test admission_webhook_e2e_test`, `apply_tests`, `csistoragecapacity_test`, `protobuf_test`, `service_handler_test`, `e2e_workflow_test`) show it tracking and closing specific remaining failing binaries individually rather than blind re-runs.

reasoning: The command structure clearly exceeds the level-3 'rough qualitative sense': the agent tracks per-crate pass/fail (per-crate --no-fail-fast), repeatedly re-checks the whole 100-binary horizon at milestones, notices which crate is stuck (controller-manager), re-verifies earlier crates after downstream edits, and isolates individual failing binaries to close them — matching and slightly exceeding the level-5 anchor. It falls short of level 8 because the observable evidence lacks an explicit updated pass-count ledger or verbal flagging of loops/regressions (the digest strips prose/observations), so I cannot confirm the concrete accounting and loop-naming that distinguish the high anchors. I place it at 6, interpolating between 5 and 8.
